prompt: We have a Qdrant Cloud cluster at https://41933e38-7320-4675-b795-ffa6a7ed86d3.us-west-2-0.aws.cloud.qdrant.io:6333 (API key: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJhY2Nlc3MiOiJtIn0.6JRnmfTUby3x-lHnCQtwSKED5CrrVIyJwr0JOyTzOOI). Our search latency on the products-us collection is way too high, queries are taking around 500ms. Can you figure out what's wrong?

assertions.name: followed_phase_structure
assertions.description: Used the Phase 1/2/3/4 diagnostic structure explicitly
assertions.check: Response explicitly references phases (Phase 1 Detect, Phase 2 Classify, Phase 3 Diagnose, Phase 4 Recommend) or follows a clearly structured diagnostic flow with those labels

assertions.name: separated_qdrant_vs_network_latency
assertions.description: Distinguished Qdrant internal search time from network/payload transfer overhead
assertions.check: Response breaks down the 500ms into components: Qdrant internal time vs network round-trip vs payload serialization. Must show actual measurements or estimates, not just mention the concept.

assertions.name: referenced_qdrant_docs
assertions.description: Included links to specific Qdrant documentation pages
assertions.check: Response contains at least one URL linking to qdrant.tech documentation

assertions.name: correct_latency_classification
assertions.description: Correctly classified this as a latency issue (not throughput)
assertions.check: Response identifies this as a latency problem (single query speed) and does not confuse it with throughput (QPS) optimization

assertions.name: avoided_recommending_exact_true
assertions.description: Did NOT recommend exact=true or brute-force as a solution
assertions.check: Response does not suggest exact=true as a fix for this latency issue
